topics.topic: Authorization checks applied when reading a snapshot import result by import_id
questions: For a read by `import_id`, does the route execute only bearer authentication and ownership lookup, or does it also execute producer-scope, grant, capability, and Registry checks from steps 2–5?
Which preceding steps apply to an import-result read, and does that read bypass producer scope, project grant and Registry checks as R0-21 requires?
Does the import-result route proceed directly from bearer authentication to `get_snapshot_import_result`, skipping all project-scope and Registry checks, or must it execute steps 2–3?

quotes: A producer's read of its own import result checks only its bearer credential and that it made the import (R0-21).

The read needs only the authenticated bearer credential of that principal: it does not recheck the producer's project grant or the Registry lifecycle, so a result stays readable after the grant is revoked or the project archived (Factory code `application/snapshot_import.py`).
judgement.why: State 0 explicitly requires the result-read route to skip producer-scope, grant, capability and Registry lifecycle checks after bearer authentication.

topics.topic: Failure representation and concealment for missing or cross-project expense/document mutation targets
questions: How are missing and cross-project expense/document targets represented, and must the two cases be concealed as the same response?
How are unknown and cross-project expense/document identifiers reported, and must both cases be concealed as the same result?
What declared failure and HTTP outcome must each expense-management mutation produce for a missing or cross-project target?

judgement.why: P3 judged the same missing-or-cross-project expense and document mutation question on unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: Classification of missing or cross-project expense and document targets
quotes: `ExpenseConflictError` for an expense of no or another project.
`ExpenseConflictError` for a document of no or another project.
precedent.why: State 5 assigns `ExpenseConflictError` to absent or cross-project expenses and documents, which the route policy maps to 409.

topics.topic: Handling and classification of authorization changes after the route-level snapshot access check
questions: After the route-level access check succeeds, what happens if the repeated authorization fails because the principal, grant, project lifecycle or Registry availability changed, especially when no ImportRejectReason represents that failure?

For each post-route authorization failure not represented by `unknown_project`, `archived_project`, or an explicitly defined scope denial, is the attempt recorded with a fresh `import_id`, and if so under which closed `ImportRejectReason`, or is an access error returned with no record?

quotes:
R0-04 and R0-25: it is reached only after the route's own
`authorize_producer_scope` and `authorize_snapshot_import` passed, so an
access refusal never reaches it and is recorded nowhere (Q20). One
fingerprint and one `occurred_at` per attempt; every classified attempt — a
content rejection (A7 contract version, A9 currency, completeness,
sections), acceptance, equal replay, differing replay, or an archived,
unknown or scope-denied project from its repeated `authorize_snapshot_import`
(called once before the transaction; only if access changed after the
route's check) — appends exactly one fresh record and one `snapshot.import`
audit in one transaction.

`AuthenticationRejected` and infrastructure failures outside the catalogue
re-raise with nothing written; every business rejection is an answered
record, not an exception.
judgement.why: State 5 decides that post-route archived, unknown and scope-denied changes become recorded results, while authentication and infrastructure failures propagate with no record.

topics.topic: Auditing credential revocations caused by replacement or viewer-revocation cascades
questions: When issuing a replacement credential or revoking a viewer automatically revokes existing credentials, is each credential revocation also recorded as `viewer.credential_revoke`, or is only the top-level issue/viewer-revoke action audited?

quotes:
`capability:viewer_access.issue_viewer_access` revokes every earlier
   credential of the viewer and its active sessions, stores the hash of one
   new secret (`capability:credential_security.issue_verification_secret`) and
   appends `viewer.credential_issue`; the plaintext link secret is in this
   answer only.

`capability:viewer_access.revoke_viewer` revokes the viewer with its
   sessions and credentials and appends `viewer.revoke`; all its projects
   close.
judgement.why: State 4 assigns one top-level audit action to each cascade: credential replacement records viewer.credential_issue and viewer revocation records viewer.revoke.

topics.topic: Idempotent result and auditing of repeated viewer credential revocation
questions: What does a second revocation of the same existing ViewerAccessCredential return, and does it append another `viewer.credential_revoke` audit record?

quotes:
Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for an unknown or already
revoked credential.

Updates the credential and every session of its viewer; appends one
`AuditRecord`.
judgement.why: State 5 makes a repeated credential revocation a ScopedNotFoundError, so it performs no update and appends no additional revocation audit.

topics.topic: Ownership of snapshot-import orchestration between the HTTP route and use case
questions: Does the import route orchestrate authentication, scope authorization, project authorization and import itself, or must one owning use case perform that orchestration behind the route?

judgement.why: P16 judged the same question about route authorization calls versus the single owning business operation on unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: Whether HTTP routes call authorization and business logic separately or through one owning use case
quotes:
A route handler extracts the
credential and the declared body, runs the route's `authorize` steps, calls
exactly one owning operation and returns its result or a safe projection;
it decides, retries and audits nothing.
precedent.why: State 5 distinguishes route authorization steps from the single owning business operation, so the handler may call the guard and then exactly one owning operation.

topics.topic: Transport-guard failure HTTP statuses and response bodies
questions: What HTTP status and response body does each transport-guard failure produce for an untrusted host, oversized body, invalid viewer-mutation origin, and rate-limited viewer entry?

quotes:
For every request, in order: a request id with no identity in it; 400 for an
untrusted host; CORS preflight 204 for a listed origin and 403 for another;
403 for a viewer logout from another origin than the public one; 413 for a
body over `max_request_body_bytes`; 429 for viewer entries over the
monotonic-clock rate limit, before any credential is parsed; then the route,
called once.
Its refusals are the statuses above, each with an empty body.
judgement.why: State 5 specifies every listed transport refusal's HTTP status and requires an empty response body.
